properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED WHILE PLANNED, AND NOW DATED — Anthony's call 2026-07-31, taken with the other three of its kind as one judgement.

The gap's literal question — "how will you confirm it?" — is ALREADY ANSWERED: ver:session-artifacts is written and sits at `planned`, pinning that THE LINK IS THE FILTER (a rendering a Decision or Capability points at is captured; one nothing points at is not, so the store does not fill with session litter) and that capture happens WITHOUT the agent choosing to invoke it, which is the load-bearing half — a rule depending on the agent remembering decays exactly as req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session measures. What the gap reports is that the check has never RUN, which is true of anything unbuilt.

WHY ACCEPT RATHER THAN LEAVE OPEN: these four were the only notes on the gate, so every cut printed "5 notes" with no way to tell signal from permanent background. When the capability is built and its check passes, the gap disappears on its own.

*** CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME DAY, LEFT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY. *** This rationale originally claimed `cap:review-expires-on-content` would bring the gap back if the capability were reworded. THAT IS FALSE — that capability is PLANNED, NOT BUILT. Expiry keys on the gap id, which hashes affected node IDS, so a review expires when the affected SET changes membership and NEVER on CONTENT change. This review does NOT self-expire; reword the capability and someone must revisit it BY HAND. Demonstrated live the same hour on the sibling acknowledgement decision:ack:4f9dcb95353889c2, where a substantial rewrite left the old judgement suppressing the gap against new text.

WHY IT IS SCHEDULED AND NOT MERELY ACCEPTED: all four were scheduled against NOTHING, so quieting them would have relied on memory. Now SCHEDULED_FOR rel:v0210 as `expected`, so arrival_delta asks at v0.21.0 regardless. `expected` and not `required`: a plan, not an obligation whose miss is a computed violation.

NOTE THE DEPENDENCY WHEN IT IS BUILT: its own description says the capture must be TRIGGERED rather than remembered, which places it with cap:skill-triggers rather than beside it — the two are scheduled into the same increment for that reason, not by coincidence.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN v0.20.0, which Anthony scoped to cap:changelog-view alone.
